title: standings(2019, serie-a) returns 21 rows: Club Athletico Paranaense split into two clubs
evidence: _factual.json raw: rank 12 'Athletico Paranaense' (matches=27) + rank 21 'Atletico Paranaense' (matches=11) = one club, 38 matches, split by spelling. soccer.cpp:35-47 normalize() strips accents and a trailing 2-letter state suffix but does NOT unify the archaic 'Athletico' (with h) vs 'Atletico'; soccer.cpp:69-73 standings() keys the table on that normalized name, so the two spellings land in separate rows. This is a factual-accuracy defect (factual_accuracy=0.5 in scores.json), NOT a missing R9 capability.
suggestion: Canonicalize 'athletico'->'atletico' (drop the intervocalic 'h') in normalize(), or add a club-alias map. Also extend tests.cpp:22 to exercise competition='serie-a' (currently only 'Brasileirao' is asserted), so this split is caught by the suite.

title: Standings test only covers Brasileirao, never the serie-a dataset path
evidence: tests.cpp:22-27 asserts db.standings(2019,'Brasileirao').size()==20 with 38 played each. The Brasileirao_Matches.csv source spells clubs consistently so this passes, but the serie-a query hits BR-Football-Dataset.csv (competition column r[0], loaded at soccer.cpp:56) where 'Athletico'/'Atletico' spellings are mixed — that path is never asserted, so the F1 defect ships green.
suggestion: Add an assertion for standings(2019,'serie-a') expecting 20 rows to close the gap.

title: R10 aggregate stats present via team_statistics location filter + win_rate
evidence: soccer.cpp:63 team_record() with location home/away/all supports home-vs-away splits; main.cpp:19 record_json computes win_rate. No dedicated avg-goals-per-match tool, but the requirement ('at least one aggregate statistic') is satisfied.
suggestion: Optional: expose an explicit league-wide aggregate (avg goals/match, biggest win) tool.
